experiment.name: Do the DS05 residual axes recur in other files? Tucker congruence by shared variable block
experiment.description: Does the correlation pattern of the DS05 residual axes recur in DS03 (red cells), S-CB050 (leukocytes) and S-CB017 (B. canis leukocytes and platelets)? Hypothesis: at least one axis recurs with congruence of 0.85 or more and a pattern more specific than chance.

parameters.stage_covariate: log(illness_days + 1) (owner-reported); SV-01 pseudo-stage failed validation and is used only in sensitivities S2 and S3
parameters.note: DS03 natural dogs are S-CB050 dogs (SV-07): the two B. rossi targets are one source

experiment.summary: No DS05 residual axis meets the replication rule (0 of 6 axis-by-block checks replicated). Block patterns recur (phi 0.99 DS03 red cell, n 103; 1.00 S-CB050 leukocytes, n 141) but cannot be shown specific with 3 variables; in the one testable block (S-CB017, B. canis, n 31) phi 0.99 is no better than a uniform pattern (0.98; label-permutation p 0.075).

results.title: Congruence of DS05 and target block patterns

payload.caption: Tucker phi with 2,000-bootstrap 95% intervals (dogs resampled in both files). Uniform: phi of the target pattern with equal loadings. Label permutation: exact, over all orderings of the target variables. DS03 and S-CB050 are one source (SRC-A, SV-07); S-CB017 is B. canis (one species per source).

results.title: Replication rule by axis and block

payload.rule: R1 retained and stable; R2 axis maps onto the block (|phi| >= 0.85); R3 phi >= 0.85, lower bound >= 0.70; R4 label-permutation p <= 0.05 and above the uniform baseline (only with 4 or more variables).

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Do the two DS05 residual axes recur in files from other sources, or are they specific to one clinic?

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: For each target, the variables shared with DS05 form a block: red cells in DS03 natural infection (MCHC, reticulocytes, ARC; n 103), leukocytes and platelets in S-CB017 day 1 (B. canis; segmented and band neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, platelets; n 31), and leukocytes in S-CB050 (WBC, segmented and band neutrophils; n 141). Both files were residualised on haematocrit where the target has it (not S-CB050). The block's principal components were compared by Tucker's phi, with bootstrap intervals, a uniform-pattern baseline and an exact label permutation.
SV-07 found that DS03 natural dogs are S-CB050 dogs, so the two B. rossi targets are one source (SRC-A), not two replications. Both are independent of DS05 (SRC-F).

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: DS03 red cell block: phi 0.99 (+0.97 to +1.00); the pattern (MCHC against reticulocytes and ARC) is far from uniform (0.40) but with 3 variables the smallest possible permutation p is 1/6, so specificity cannot be tested. The pattern is close to arithmetic: reticulocytes have a low MCHC.
S-CB050 leukocyte block: phi 1.00 (+0.99 to +1.00), but a uniform pattern gives 0.99: three counts that are parts of one another load together in any file.

S-CB017 block, the only one where specificity is testable: component 1 phi 0.99 (+0.85 to +1.00), uniform 0.98, label-permutation p 0.075 (120 orderings): not specific. Component 2 (platelets against the leukocytes) phi 0.77 (+0.17 to +0.93), p 0.017, below the 0.85 threshold.

By the rule stated in advance, 0 of 6 axis-by-block checks replicate and 4 are congruent but not specific. Also, the shared blocks hold at most two of the step-1 variables in the B. rossi files, so they cannot tell axis 1 from axis 2: both map onto each block.

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: A negative result here is mostly a limit of the files: the targets share 3 to 5 variables with DS05, too few to recover a 12-variable axis. It does not show that the DS05 axes are clinic-specific. The S-CB017 comparison crosses species and source (one species per source), so a failure there cannot be read as a species difference. No subtype and no predictive score.
